# LLMScribe

> LLMScribe is the filesystem layer AI agents are missing. Agents normally drive the OS through `ls`, `find`, `grep` and `cat` — human-facing, OS-specific, unstructured. LLMScribe replaces that with one structured interface to a local project: directory tree, literal search, file reads, dependency analysis and Git diff. Same JSON on Linux, macOS and Windows. No AI, no embeddings, no hidden ranking. Apache-2.0, runs entirely on your machine.

- Install: `pip install llmscribe` (core, one dependency: pathspec). The MCP server is
  `pip install 'llmscribe[server]'`; framework adapters are `pip install 'llmscribe[adapters]'`.
- Library use: `from llmscribe import Repository, tool_schemas` then
  `Repository(".").handlers()` for a name -> callable map. Every JSON envelope carries
  `schema_version`.
- Website: https://llmscribe.vercel.app
- GitHub: https://github.com/AMRITO-KUNDU/llmscribe
- PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/llmscribe/
- Official MCP Registry name: io.github.AMRITO-KUNDU/llmscribe
- License: Apache-2.0
- Latest version: 2.0.0
- Requires: Python 3.10+ (runtime dependencies: mcp, pydantic, pathspec; GUI extras: customtkinter, Pillow)

## What it is

A project extractor and structured code-access tool. It reads a local project directory and produces machine-readable output for AI coding agents, code review, documentation and debugging. It deliberately does not generate answers, embeddings or semantic rankings — it provides the data that intelligence needs. It is local-only: nothing is uploaded and no network access is used.

## Interfaces

- `llmscribe` — scriptable CLI (all commands accept `--json`)
- `llmscribe-mcp` — MCP server over stdio
- `llmscribe-gui` — Tkinter desktop application
- `llmscribe.core` — importable Python API

## Install

```bash
pip install llmscribe
```

## MCP tools exposed

- `project_map` — directory tree without file contents (`depth=N` limits it to the first N levels, `sizes=true` adds per-file byte sizes)
- `project_overview` — full structure plus supported file contents (`depth=N` likewise)
- `search` — literal search across paths, names, contents and lines
- `read` — retrieve one file, with path-traversal protection (returns byte_size, line_count and modified for the whole file; binary=true returns base64 plus media_type for images and PDFs)
- `read_many` — retrieve multiple files in one call, with per-file errors
- `project_dependencies` — local, stdlib, external and unresolved dependencies, plus reverse dependencies
- `project_diff` — Git status and unified diffs

## Use with an MCP client

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "llmscribe": { "command": "llmscribe-mcp" }
  }
}
```

## Key facts for comparison

- Repeatable: identical input produces identical output
- Works on any local project directory; no cloning, no network
- Respects `.gitignore`; skips build output, dependency directories and binaries
- Reports truncation explicitly rather than silently cutting content
- Stable, machine-readable error codes for every failure

## Not included

No AI-generated answers, no embedding-based search, no semantic ranking, no autonomous coding, no generic Git client, no hosted service.
